description: A line plot comparing two querying methods: 'Collapsed tree' (green line) and 'Tree Traversal' (blue line). The x-axis represents 'Context Length' ranging from 0 to 2500, and the y-axis represents 'F1' ranging from 40 to 60. The 'Collapsed tree' line rises sharply to a peak around 2000 context length (approx 59 F1) and then declines. The 'Tree Traversal' line rises more gradually, peaking around 2000-2500 context length (approx 57-58 F1). The 'Collapsed tree' line is consistently above the 'Tree Traversal' line for context lengths greater than approximately 250.

The figure displays three line plots arranged horizontally, each showing 'Prompt + Completion Tokens' on the y-axis versus 'Document Length (Tokens)' on the x-axis. The plots correspond to three datasets: Qasper (red line), Narrative QA (blue line), and Quality (green line). In all three plots, the lines exhibit a generally upward trend, indicating that token costs increase as document length increases.

A line plot showing 'Time in seconds' on the y-axis (ranging from 0 to 1500) versus 'Length of document in tokens' on the x-axis (ranging from 0 to 80000). The plot displays a single green line with data points that generally trend upwards, indicating an increase in time as document length increases. There is a noticeable dip in the line between approximately 30,000 and 40,000 tokens.

A composite image containing four bar charts. The top row displays three smaller charts side-by-side for datasets NarrativeQA, Quality, and Qasper. The bottom section displays three larger, clearer charts for the same datasets. Each chart plots 'Percentage' on the y-axis against 'Layer' on the x-axis. The bars represent three retrievers: SBERT (blue), BM25 (green), and DPR (red).

A diagram illustrating the RAPTOR tree construction process, divided into three panels. The left panel shows a 'RAPTOR Tree' with a 'Leaf layer' (nodes 1-5) and a 'Root layer' (nodes 9-10), connected by lines. The middle panel details the 'Formation of one tree layer', showing 'Text chunks' (1-5) being grouped into clusters (e.g., 3 & 5, 1 & 4 & 5) and then summarized by an LLM to form parent nodes (6, 7, 8). The right panel, titled 'Contents of a node', lists the attributes of a node: Index #8, Child Nodes: 2, 3, Text: summary of nodes 2 and 3, and Text Embedding.

A diagram illustrating two methods for query formulation: 'implicit query by masking' and 'explicit query by question generation'. The implicit method shows a sentence with specific phrases underlined and then masked out. The explicit method shows the underlined phrases being converted into questions via a neural network icon labeled 'LM such as ChatGPT'.

A grouped bar chart comparing four retrieval methods (No ret., Single-time ret., Previous-window ret., and FLARE) across five datasets: 2WikiMultihopQA, StrategyQA, ASQA, ASQA-hint, and WikiAsp. The y-axis represents the score, ranging from 0.0 to 80.0. Each dataset group contains four bars corresponding to the methods, with specific numerical values labeled on top of each bar.

A line plot showing the performance (EM) of two datasets, 2WikiMultihopQA (blue line) and StrategyQA (red line), as a function of the percentage of steps/sentences with retrieval. The x-axis ranges from 0.0 to 100.0, and the y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 80.0. The plot displays data points at 0%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% retrieval. The 2WikiMultihopQA line starts at 28.2 and rises to 51.0. The StrategyQA line starts at 72.9, rises to a peak of 77.3 at 25%, and then slightly decreases to 73.4 at 100%.

A scatter plot showing QA performance (F1) on the y-axis (range 20-50) versus Time per Query on the x-axis (range 0-10). Four methods are plotted: 'No Retrieval' (blue x, ~0.5 time, ~21 F1), 'Adaptive Retrieval' (green x, ~1 time, ~32 F1), 'Single-step Approach' (orange x, ~1.5 time, ~44 F1), 'Adaptive-RAG (Ours)' (purple star, ~3.5 time, ~48 F1), and 'Multi-step Approach' (red x, ~8.5 time, ~49 F1).

A conceptual diagram comparing three retrieval-augmented LLM approaches: (A) Single-Step, (B) Multi-Step, and (C) Adaptive. Panel (A) shows a single retrieval step for both simple and complex queries. Panel (B) shows iterative retrieval (labeled 'k times') for both query types, marked as 'Inefficient'. Panel (C) shows a 'Classifier' routing different query types (Straightforward, Simple, Complex) to different processing paths: direct answer, single retrieval, or iterative retrieval.
